source_refs.quote: sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession
These three expressions deal with different concepts and apply to different circumstances.

In subletting there exists the relationship of landlord and tenant as between the tenant and his sub-tenant and all the incidents of letting or tenancy have to be found, namely the transfer of an interest in the estate payment of rent, and the right to possession as against the tenant in respect of the Premises sublet.
In assignment the tenant has to divest himself of all the rights that he has as a tenant.
there must be vesting of possession by the tenant in another person by divesting himself not only of physical possession but also of the right to possession
The divestment or abandonment of the right to possession is necessary in order to invoke the clause of parting with possession
If there is anything in the nature of a right to concurrent user there is no parting with possession
The mere user by other persons is no parting with Possession so long as the tenant retains the legal possession himself

nodes.text: It is alleged that the respondent tenant is not in possession and that a sub-tenant is in exclusive possession of the tenancy shop

nodes.text: The respondent denies having sub-let, assigned, or otherwise parted with the tenancy premises and denies that an alleged sub-tenant is in possession

source_refs.quote: It is wrong and is denied that the respondent has Sub- letted, assigned or otherwise parted with the tenancy premises or the respondent is not in possession thereof or that it is any alleged sub-tenant who is in possession of the tenancy shop.

nodes.text: The respondent states that he himself is in use, occupation, and possession of the tenanted shop

nodes.text: The petitioners sought to prove that the respondent had sub-let the shop to Arun Sood

source_refs.quote: the prime effort of the petitioners to prove that the respondent had sub- let the shop to his son Arun Sood

nodes.text: The petitioners sought to prove that Arun Sood was in exclusive use of the premises and was running his business in the name and style of M/s Sood Store

source_refs.quote: and that he was in exclusive use of the premises, running his business in the name and style of M/s Sood Store.

nodes.text: Photographs depict a Sood Stores sign board displayed across the subject premises

nodes.text: The record states that the respondent, in his evidence, did not deny the presence of his son Arun Sood in the premises

nodes.text: The respondent's case is that he continues to be in possession and control of the tenanted shop

source_refs.quote: If there is anything in the nature of a right to concurrent user there is no parting with possession
The mere user by other persons is no parting with Possession so long as the tenant retains the legal possession himself
A tenant cannot be said to part with the possession of any part of the premises unless his agreement with the license wholly ousts him from the legal possession of that part.
